government.note: Releasable country. On 1 January 2000 Kosovo was administered by the United Nations Interim Administration Mission in Kosovo (UNMIK) under the Special Representative of the Secretary-General (SRSG), the effective executive here. The lists of Kosovo's presidents and prime ministers record the parallel institutions of the self-proclaimed Republic of Kosova (President Ibrahim Rugova from 1992, Prime Minister Bujar Bukoshi from 1991) and a provisional government with Hashim Thaçi as prime minister from April 1999, all ending on 1 February 2000; UNMIK set up its Joint Interim Administrative Structure in January 2000. The Provisional Institutions of Self-Government followed: an Assembly elected in November 2001, which elected a President and a Prime Minister in March 2002. Kosovo declared independence on 17 February 2008; the 2008 Constitution provides for a President elected by the Assembly (two-thirds in the first two rounds, a simple majority of all members in the third) and a Government responsible to the 120-member Assembly. The type field keeps the 2000 value.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Estimate: there was no Kosovo-wide vote before 2000 that UNMIK recognised, so the shares of the first Assembly election (17 November 2001) are used: LDK 45.7% (liberal conservative), PDK 25.7% and AAK 7.8% (national conservative), the Serb Return Coalition 11.3% and other minority lists 3.5% (regionalist), LKÇK and LPK 1.7% (ethno-nationalist), the Albanian Christian Democratic Party 1.0% (Christian democrat); remaining lists about 3.4% (big tent).
